title: Orthonormal real eigenbasis for a symmetric linear operator
statement: Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional real inner product space [def-weil-finite-dimensional-subspace]: a real vector space with a symmetric bilinear form $\langle-,-\rangle$ such that $\langle v,v\rangle>0$ for $v\ne0$, equipped with its induced norm $\|v\|=\sqrt{\langle v,v\rangle}$. Let $n=\dim_{\mathbf R}V$, and let $T:V\to V$ be a real linear map satisfying $\langle Tx,y\rangle=\langle x,Ty\rangle$ for all $x,y\in V$. Then there are real numbers $a_1,\ldots,a_n$ and an orthonormal basis $e_1,\ldots,e_n$ of $V$ such that $Te_i=a_i e_i$ for every $i$. Orthonormal means $\langle e_i,e_j\rangle=1$ if $i=j$ and $0$ otherwise; the zero-dimensional space and empty basis are included.
